tips.name: Sulfate-free wash
tips.advice: Choose a sulfate-free shampoo or cleansing conditioner so you don't strip the natural oils 4C hair needs.

tips.name: Watch your silicones
tips.advice: Non-water-soluble silicones such as dimethicone can build up and block moisture. Check labels, or clarify when buildup appears.

tips.name: Low manipulation
tips.advice: Keep styling simple. Less combing and handling means less breakage on fragile 4C strands.

tips.name: Finger detangle
tips.advice: Detangle on damp hair coated in conditioner, using fingers or a wide-tooth comb from the ends upward.

tips.name: Satin at night
tips.advice: Protect your hair overnight with a satin bonnet or pillowcase to cut friction and moisture loss.

tips.name: Layer your moisture
tips.advice: High porosity hair loses moisture fast. Layer a water-based leave-in, then a cream, then seal with a butter or heavier oil.

tips.name: Protein balance
tips.advice: A gentle protein treatment now and then can help fill gaps in the cuticle. Follow it with a moisturising deep conditioner.

tips.name: Go easy on heat
tips.advice: Heat and very hot water can lift the cuticle further. Use lukewarm water and a heat protectant.

tips.name: Warm deep condition
tips.advice: Low porosity hair resists moisture. Deep condition with gentle heat, such as a warm towel or steamer, so the cuticle lifts and the product absorbs.

tips.name: Go lightweight
tips.advice: Heavy butters can sit on top of low porosity hair. Choose lightweight oils like jojoba or grapeseed and thin, water-based products.

tips.name: Apply to damp hair
tips.advice: Apply products to warm, damp hair in small amounts. Use less than you think you need, since low porosity hair gets weighed down easily.

tips.name: Clarify monthly
tips.advice: Product buildup is common with low porosity hair. A monthly clarifying wash helps moisture get back in.
